old: Kings often carry traditional epithets introduced by *úgy nevezték, mint...* (he was referred to as...) or *a nép ...-ként emlegette* (people referred to him as...). Legal acts use transitive past verbs like *megerősített* (confirmed) and *bevezetett* (introduced).
new: You know *-ként* (\"as\") from A2 Unit 36 and the past tense from earlier units. Here they appear in set history phrases: *Nagy Lajosnak nevezték* (they called him Louis the Great), *lovagkirályként tisztelték* (they honoured him as a knight-king), *megerősítette az Aranybullát* (he confirmed the Golden Bull) and *bevezette az ősiség törvényét* (he introduced the law of entailment).
why: *úgy nevezték, mint* is not natural Hungarian; recap of known forms instead.
